Marginal material
At the far left, beside approximately lines 13–14, there are cropped dark letter fragments. They are too incomplete to transcribe or securely assign to this column. No separate full marginal line is visible.

Visible interventions and marks
A thin oblique stroke crosses text near the left portion of the cropped first line and the beginning of line 2. Its function is uncertain.
There is a conspicuous slash between the uncertain hoī̄s reading and Quid on line 6, with a small raised dark mark above the latter part of Quid. I cannot establish whether that raised mark is an insertion, an abbreviation, or incidental marking.
A cross-shaped mark stands between asini and sic on line 12; its vertical stroke extends downward toward line 13. I have represented it by + without interpreting its function.
Dark oblique strokes and a small opaque dark patch affect the left portion of lines 15–16. These obscure letters. I cannot confidently distinguish cancellation, later annotation, and damage there.
Other fine strokes occur above or through letters, including near line 16 at the right. I cannot securely identify a deleted word or a legible interlinear addition. No deletion has been silently resolved.

Limitations
Only one image was supplied, so no overlap with another crop can be assessed. The first and last lines are cut off. The left margin is also cropped, and some letters and abbreviation strokes are difficult to distinguish at this scale. Text is visible as one main column; there is no evidence in this image sufficient to reconstruct neighboring columns or their order.

This reading is substantially uncertain, especially in the upper four lines, line 6, and parts of lines 9 and 14–16. Some apparent letters may instead be abbreviation marks. Uncertain forms have not been completed from grammatical or philosophical expectations. The hyphen after reci on line 13 is an editorial indication of the apparent physical word division before pit on line 14, not a securely visible manuscript hyphen.
